_comment: Quality floors for fbtberger-raft. Both numbers may only go UP -- see the kwatro repository's QUALITY.md. Pitest is pointed at the arithmetic the protocol rests on (Quorum, RaftConfig, storage), not at RaftNode: one mutant there means booting a cluster.
_coverage_note: LOWERED from 0.4635193 to 0.46 on 2026-08-30, deliberately, and this is the commit that says why. That number was never reproducible: five measurements in one sitting gave 4211, 4211, 4200, 4200 and 4200 covered lines out of 9087 -- a spread of twelve lines, 46.22 % to 46.34 % -- and the recorded floor of 4212 was the high-water mark of that spread from an earlier session. It only ever passed because coverageRatchet was reading a report from an OLDER run: the task read a file another task writes, and nothing ordered the two. Fixing that ordering (see gradle/ratchet.gradle.kts) is what made the ratchet read this run's measurement and fail. The spread itself is real and is not the ratchet's fault -- this repository's tests drive elections and timeouts, so different runs walk different branches. A floor has to sit under the whole spread or it tears at random, which is a ratchet nobody can commit through. Raise it once the measurement is stable, not before.
